subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose resetSessionEntryLifecycle as the supported Plugin SDK contract for channel-driven external lifecycle boundaries, including owner-coordinated resets of locked harness sessions?
rationale: The code and proof support the Teams fix, but shipping the method commits OpenClaw to a new compatibility-sensitive plugin API and a specific ownership model for interrupting and rotating session state.

options.title: Approve the owner-aware SDK contract
options.body: Accept the new generic lifecycle-reset API and its harness handoff semantics, then refresh the branch and complete exact-head merge validation.

options.title: Keep the reset internal
options.body: Refactor the Teams fix onto a bundled-only or narrower core seam so third-party plugins do not receive a permanent general reset API.

options.title: Pause the behavior change
options.body: Do not merge until maintainers choose a different retention policy or session-boundary contract for Teams uninstall events.

recommendation.title: Approve the owner-aware SDK contract
recommendation.body: Accept the new generic lifecycle-reset API and its harness handoff semantics, then refresh the branch and complete exact-head merge validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They already authored the commit defining the personal-chat scope and are the clearest available decision owner for this PR's permanent API and behavior boundary.
